descriptionChirho: Hifil causative sense: to prepare, make ready, or provide something in advance; Arabic أَعَدَّ / هَيَّأَ confirms the 'preparation' meaning across all inflections.
Hifil causative sense: to establish, set up, or make firm a kingdom, throne, or person; Arabic ثَبَّتَ / أَقَامَ distinguishes this from mere preparation.
Nifal passive/stative sense: to be established, stand firm, or endure; Arabic يَثْبُتُ / تَثْبُتُ indicates a state of firmness or permanence.
Nifal participle as adjective: ready, prepared for action or an event; Arabic مُسْتَعِدّ and Swahili tayari confirm readiness rather than firmness.
Nifal participle as adjective: what is right, correct, certain, or true; Arabic صَوَابًا / صِدْقٌ / يَقِين distinguishes this ethical-epistemic sense from physical firmness.
Piel intensive sense: to establish firmly, confirm, or found; Arabic ثَبَّتَ / أَسَّسَ indicates deliberate, intensive strengthening or founding action.
Pual and Hofal passive senses: to be established, be prepared, or be set in place by another agent; Arabic مُعَدّ / يُثَبَّتُ confirms the passive construction.
Hitpael reflexive-passive sense: to establish oneself, be established, or prepare oneself; Arabic يَسْتَعِدّ / تُثَبَّتِينَ indicates self-directed or reflexive establishment.
Extended sense of directing or aiming toward a target; Arabic تُصَوِّبُ (aim) and Swahili kuelekeza (direct) distinguish this from preparation or establishment.
Nifal sense of physical forming or shaping, as of bodily development; Arabic نَهَدَ (swell/form) marks this as a distinct physical-developmental meaning.
Hifil infinitive absolute used adverbially to intensify the verb, meaning firmly or steadfastly; functions as an adverbial modifier rather than a finite verbal sense.
Piel sense of fitting or setting in place, specifically of arrows on the bowstring or similar preparation of implements for use; Arabic أَعَدُّوا in the context of weapon preparation.
